label: Смотреть
description: A full conjugation deck for смотреть: present persons, past, future, the high-value imperative смотри, and на+acc government.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: First-person present. 1. 'Смотрю' is the я-form of смотреть. 2. 'Интересный фильм' is a direct object in the accusative. 3. This is the core pattern смотреть + accusative.
Strategic focus: Second-person present. 1. 'Смотришь' is the ты-form. 2. 'Телевизор' is an accusative object. 3. 'Часто' adds frequency to this casual everyday action.

missions.phrase: Этот мальчик пристально смотрит на меня.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Third-person present. 1. 'Смотрит' is the он/она-form. 2. 'На меня' uses смотреть на + accusative meaning to look at. 3. This is a key government pattern.
Strategic focus: Third-person present with в. 1. 'Смотрит' is the она-form. 2. 'В окно' uses смотреть в + accusative meaning to look into. 3. This trains directional government.
Strategic focus: First-person plural. 1. 'Смотрим' is the мы-form. 2. 'Новости' is a plural accusative object. 3. 'Каждый вечер' frames this common daily routine.
Strategic focus: Polite/plural form. 1. 'Смотрите' is the respectful вы-form. 2. 'Новый спектакль' is an accusative object. 3. This suits a formal cultural setting.
Strategic focus: Third-person plural. 1. 'Смотрят' is the они-form. 2. 'Важный матч' is an accusative object. 3. This completes all six present persons.
Strategic focus: Masculine past. 1. 'Смотрел' is the masculine past of смотреть. 2. 'Вчера' anchors the action in the past. 3. The speaker is male here.
Strategic focus: Feminine past. 1. 'Смотрела' is the feminine past. 2. 'На детей' uses смотреть на + accusative. 3. The subject is female.

Strategic focus: Neuter past. 1. 'Смотрело' is the neuter past, agreeing with neuter 'окно'. 2. 'Окно смотрело во двор' is a real Russian idiom for a window facing somewhere. 3. This trains rare neuter agreement.

missions.phrase: В субботу мы смотрели хорошее кино.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Plural past. 1. 'Смотрели' is the plural past for any gender mix. 2. 'Кино' is an indeclinable accusative object. 3. This completes the four past forms.

missions.phrase: Завтра я буду смотреть важный матч.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Imperfective future. 1. 'Буду смотреть' is буду plus the infinitive. 2. 'Важный матч' is an accusative object. 3. This expresses an ongoing future action.
Strategic focus: Singular imperative. 1. 'Смотри' is the command form of смотреть. 2. Here it draws attention to something striking. 3. This is a very high-value everyday word.
Strategic focus: Plural imperative. 1. 'Смотрите' is the polite/plural command. 2. 'Сюда' means here, as a direction. 3. This is useful for getting attention.
Strategic focus: Imperative with government. 1. 'Смотри' is the singular command. 2. 'На дорогу' uses смотреть на + accusative. 3. This is a real warning to watch the road.
Strategic focus: Negated present. 1. 'Не' negates the verb смотрю. 2. 'Телевизор' stays accusative after a simple negation. 3. This states a habit you barely have.

missions.phrase: По утрам он смотрит в зеркало.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Government with в. 1. 'Смотрит' is the он-form. 2. 'В зеркало' uses смотреть в + accusative. 3. This trains looking into something.
Strategic focus: Perfective future. 1. 'Посмотрю' is the perfective посмотреть, signalling a completed action. 2. 'Завтра' sets it in the future. 3. This contrasts with the imperfective.
Strategic focus: Perfective imperative. 1. 'Посмотри' is the perfective command. 2. 'На это' uses смотреть на + accusative meaning at this. 3. This asks for a quick single look.
Strategic focus: Perfective third-person. 1. 'Посмотрит' is the perfective future она-form. 2. 'В окно' uses смотреть в + accusative. 3. This implies one glance, not a process.
